close_reason: Changed QueryResult.position from i64 to u64 (and QueryResult::new's position parameter) so the response-side position cannot be constructed as a negative value. RFC 8620 §5.5 specifies UnsignedInt in the response; the request-side position parameter on query_objects remains i64 because the spec permits negative request offsets for end-relative indexing. Backend impls that compute start from a signed request offset now cast to u64 at the boundary (already non-negative by min/max clamp). Swept 7 *-server crate memory.rs backends + mail-server's email.rs and submission.rs handlers via a context-aware regex replacing 'as i64' inside QueryResult::new(...) with 'as u64' plus one literal '0i64' → '0u64'. cargo build/test/clippy/fmt --all-features clean.
description:
Path: crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:480 (`pub position: i64`) and src/handlers.rs:211 (`"position": result.position`).

RFC 8620 §5.5 defines the `/query` response field:
  position: UnsignedInt - The 0-based index of the first result in the ids array

UnsignedInt maps to u64 in this codebase's idiom (matches other use of u64 for unsigned-int wire fields throughout backend.rs: max_recipients, max_size, max_changes, etc.). QueryResult.position is i64, NOT u64.

The justification i64 makes sense in the REQUEST: RFC 8620 §5.5 says the request's position can be negative as an end-relative offset (-1 = last result). That's correctly typed as i64 on the request side — see `position: i64` parameter on query_objects at backend.rs:737.

But QueryResult is the RESPONSE shape, and the response cannot validly contain a negative position. The current type allows a backend to construct `QueryResult { position: -1, ... }` and have it serialise to the wire as JSON number `-1`. JMAP clients parsing as `UnsignedInt` will either reject with a parse error or coerce to an unexpected value depending on their lib.

Right shape: `pub position: u64` on QueryResult. Backends that need to convert from a signed request offset to the unsigned response position do so explicitly. Compile-time enforcement that the response value cannot be negative.

Caller impact when fixed: backend impls that today silently produce wire-spec-violating responses (whether by bug or by accidental sign-flip) become compile errors. Backends that currently produce correct responses just change `position: 0` → `position: 0u64` (literal infers fine; no source change).

This is a five-line change in this crate plus one-line changes in each backend impl that constructs QueryResult.
title: QueryResult.position is i64 but RFC 8620 §5.5 specifies UnsignedInt in the response — a backend returning negative position silently produces a malformed wire response
